newsitem.title: USA: Former bond trader pleads guilty to scam.
newsitem.headline: Former bond trader pleads guilty to scam.

text.p: A former bond trader who was a fugitive in Canada for three years pleaded guilty in federal court Wednesday to two counts of wire fraud in a 1992 Treasury bond futures trading scheme, prosecutors said.

A U.S. District Court will sentence Darrell Zimmerman, 35, on Dec. 17. He could receive up to eight years in prison and millions of dollars in fines and restitution. Zimmerman's lawyers said his sentence will be no more than two years, the U.S. Attorney's office here said.

Zimmerman and fellow-trader Anthony Catalfo were alleged to have lost more than $8 million in the Oct. 22, 1992 attempt to manipulate the Chicago Board of Trade's Treasury bond futures market, according to a 1993 federal indictment.
The two traders allegedly entered orders in the bond futures and options pits valued at more than $1 billion while telling other brokers that they would be managing large sums for outside investors.

Neither trader had the capital to stand behind their trading positions, exposing their clearing firms to huge losses when the positions were liquidated. The scheme nearly bankrupted Lee B. Stern, a privately held Chicago brokerage house.
Catalfo was convicted in 1994 and sentenced to 3-1/2 years in prison. Zimmerman fled to his native Vancouver, Canada, and was extradited to the United States in July.
